dedupe_keys.name: eia coal transportation rates to the electric power sector basin to state rail truck and waterway costs 2008 2024

description: Coal Transportation Rates to the Electric Power Sector is an EIA statistical release of what power plants pay to move coal, with final data through 2024 released on 23 February 2026. Contents: tables of average transportation and delivered costs of coal by year and primary transport mode, average annual transportation costs from coal basin to state by truck and by railroad, state-to-state costs by waterway, and annual coal shipments to electric power plants by mode, each in nominal and real 2024 dollars. Rates are derived from Form EIA-923 Schedule 2 fuel receipts by subtracting commodity cost from delivered cost for plants of 50 MW or more, converted to dollars per ton and weighted by shipment. Producer: EIA. Coverage: United States, final rates 2008 to 2024; earlier releases back to 2001 used Surface Transportation Board waybill samples. Format and access: Excel tables on the release page with an archive of earlier years. Licence: public domain; EIA's copyright and reuse page says U.S. government publications are not subject to copyright and asks users to acknowledge the source with its publication date. Caveats: rates follow the primary mode only, exclude cogenerators and other end users, rely on EIA exclusion rules for suspect costs, and waybill-based updates stopped after the STB changed its confidentiality interpretation. Simulation uses: freight cost parameters for rail, barge and truck coal flows in energy and freight network models. Related records: data-eia-923-power-plant-operations and data-eia-us-energy-atlas-and-maps.
